info.title: WormholeSystems API
info.description:
Everything the map screen does goes over this API, and all of it is open to a script holding a personal access token. It is generated from the same handlers and wire types the frontend uses, so it is complete and current by construction.

**Pre-alpha.** The API follows the frontend and changes with it, without notice and without a migration path. Pin the version you tested against and expect to revisit.

Sign in with the session cookie a browser holds, or send `Authorization: Bearer wst_...` with a token minted under Settings, API tokens. A token acts as the user who made it, with exactly their access. Endpoints marked with no security requirement are public; the ones that also accept a share token (`?share=`) say so in their parameters.

Live updates go over WebSockets, which this document cannot describe: see `docs/realtime-api.md` in the repository.

get.summary:
`GET /api/access-subjects/search?q=`, characters, corporations and alliances that can
be granted access. Only entities WormholeSystems has already cached are searchable (a character
who has signed in, or a corp/alliance one of them belongs to), hence the UI also
accepting a raw EVE id.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: What to look for; at least two characters.

get.summary:
`GET /api/effects?name=&class=`: the buffs/debuffs a wormhole effect applies at a
system's class. Reference data, so no actor/role check.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The effect, as the map names it (`Pulsar`, `Wolf-Rayet Star`, ...).

parameters.name: class
parameters.description: The wormhole class the effect applies at.

get.summary:
`GET /api/evescout`, public Thera/Turnur connections, proxied and cached for 60s.
Upstream failures degrade to an empty list.
`GET /api/grid-config`: the server-owned map canvas geometry.

`GET /api/instance`: what this deployment has switched on. No actor check; it says
nothing an anonymous visitor could not infer from which buttons appear.
`GET /api/maps`, every map the signed-in character can access, with their role.

post.summary: `POST /api/maps`, create a map owned by the active character.

`POST /api/maps/transfer/import-new`: create a fresh map from a file, owned by the
acting character.

get.summary: `GET /api/maps/{id}`: the full map view (map + systems + connections).

parameters.name: share
parameters.description: A share token, for reading a map that was opened with a link rather than a grant.

get.summary: `GET /api/maps/{id}/access`, who can see this map, and at what role. Viewer+.

post.summary: `POST /api/maps/{id}/access/transfer`, hand the map to another character on it.

get.summary: `GET /api/maps/{id}/alerts`, every alert on the map. Manager+.

post.summary: `POST /api/maps/{id}/alerts`, create one. Manager+.

get.summary: `GET /api/maps/{id}/alerts/events`: the audit trail. Manager+.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many of the newest lines to return.

post.summary: `POST /api/maps/{id}/alerts/{alert_id}/active`, turn it on or off by hand. Manager+.

get.summary:
`GET /api/maps/{id}/background-image`: the caller's own image on this map. The `?v=`
the settings URL carries is only a cache key; the row says which file it is.

put.summary:
`PUT /api/maps/{id}/background-image`: multipart with one `image` part. Replaces the
previous image and answers with the caller's settings, URL included.

get.summary:
`GET /api/maps/{id}/characters`, presence: online characters of users who opted into
tracking on this map, holding the location scope, whose user has member-or-better
access. Member+ may view (viewers never see pilot data).

post.summary: `POST /api/maps/{id}/connections/add`
post.description:
The ghost guard sits here, not in the command: raising a ghost creates the one connection
an unmapped hole may have, and that goes through the same command from the inside.

post.summary:
`POST /api/maps/{id}/connections/clean-stale`, sweep them, and the placements they
orphan, as one undoable change.

get.summary:
`GET /api/maps/{id}/connections/stale`, edges that have been critical or expired for
over an hour.
`GET /api/maps/{id}/connections/{cid}/jumps`: the latest 10 jump-log rows.

parameters.name: share
parameters.description: A share token, for reading a map that was opened with a link rather than a grant.

get.summary: `GET /api/maps/{id}/events`: the map's history tree and where it currently sits. Viewer+.

post.summary:
`POST /api/maps/{id}/events/goto`, move the map onto any step, including one on a
branch that was left behind by an undo. Member+.
`POST /api/maps/{id}/events/redo`, step forward onto the most recent next point. Member+.

`POST /api/maps/{id}/events/undo`, step back to the previous point in the history.
Member+. Moving the cursor can touch anything the steps it crosses did, so it publishes
`HistoryChanged` and clients refetch rather than trying to reconstruct a targeted event.

`POST /api/maps/{id}/evescout/add`, put every public hole out of one hub on the map.
Member+. Answers with how many connections it added; the socket drives the refetch.

get.summary: `GET /api/maps/{id}/ignored`: the systems this map keeps out of the way.

parameters.name: share
parameters.description: A share token, for reading a map that was opened with a link rather than a grant.

200.description: How many systems were removed from the list

get.summary:
`GET /api/maps/{id}/killmails`, recent kills in this map's systems, newest first.
Viewer+, like reading the graph: a killmail is public record on zKillboard anyway.

parameters.name: solar_system_id
parameters.description:
The solar system selected on the map. Only read when the card is set to follow the
selection; the server keeps no idea of what a viewer has selected.

parameters.name: share
parameters.description: A share token, for reading a map that was opened with a link rather than a grant.

get.summary: `GET /api/maps/{id}/roles`: the map's named Discord roles. Manager+.

post.summary: `POST /api/maps/{id}/roles`, register a role to ping. Manager+.

get.summary:
`GET /api/maps/{id}/search?q=`: the map command palette. Matches placed systems by
name, alias, occupier and (for members) notes, then falls back to off-map systems the
palette can offer to add. Hits come back ranked by what matched ([`match_rank`]): a
system named like the query always beats one whose intel merely mentions it. Viewer+.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: What to look for; at least two characters.

parameters.name: share
parameters.description: A share token, for reading a map that was opened with a link rather than a grant.

get.summary:
`GET /api/maps/{id}/settings/user`: the caller's per-map preferences (defaults when
no row exists yet). Requires any access to the map.

post.summary:
`POST /api/maps/{id}/settings/user`, partial update (upsert) of the caller's per-map
preferences.
`POST /api/maps/{id}/share`, mint a share link, replacing any earlier one.

get.summary: `GET /api/maps/{id}/signatures`, all signatures on the map.

parameters.name: share
parameters.description: A share token, for reading a map that was opened with a link rather than a grant.

post.summary:
`POST /api/maps/{id}/signatures/remove-bulk`: the panel's "delete missing
signatures" path, with the legacy connection + orphan-endpoint cascade.

`POST /api/maps/{id}/systems/resolve-ghost`, say which system a ghost turned out to
be. Merging into an existing placement removes the ghost, so that goes out too.

get.summary: `GET /api/maps/{id}/systems/{mss}/details`, member-gated intel (notes). 403 for viewers.

`GET /api/maps/{id}/transfer/counts`: how much of the map each section carries.
Manager+.

`GET /api/maps/{id}/transfer/export?sections=...`: the selected sections as a JSON file
download. Manager+. A GET with a `content-disposition`, so the browser does the saving.

200.description: The export, served as a file download

post.summary:
`POST /api/maps/{id}/transfer/import`: merge a file's selected sections into the map.
Manager+.
`POST /api/maps/{id}/update`, rename a map or change its description/image. Manager+.

get.summary: `GET /api/maps/{id}/watchlist`: the map's tracked destinations.

parameters.name: share
parameters.description: A share token, for reading a map that was opened with a link rather than a grant.

get.summary: `GET /api/maps/{id}/webhooks`: the map's destinations. Manager+.

post.summary: `POST /api/maps/{id}/webhooks`, register a destination. Manager+.

delete.summary:
`DELETE /api/maps/{id}/webhooks/{webhook_id}`. Manager+. Alerts pointing at it are
deleted too, rather than left enabled with nowhere to post.

get.summary: `GET /api/me`, who's signed in, if anyone.

200.description: The acting character, or `null` when nobody is signed in

get.summary: `GET /api/me/characters`: the user's characters, marking the active and preferred ones.
`GET /api/me/discord`: the linked Discord account, if any.

post.summary: `POST /api/me/discord/unlink`, forget it, and stop what depended on it.
`POST /api/me/preferred-character`, choose which character new sessions start as.

`POST /api/me/remove-character`, remove one of the user's characters. Refuses to remove
the last one. If it's the active character, the session switches to another first (so
the session isn't cascade-deleted).

get.summary:
`GET /api/me/scopes`, every ESI permission the app can use, and whether the acting
character has granted it. Always the full list, so the UI can show what is missing.
`GET /api/me/status`, live status of the active character (online / system / ship).

200.description: The live status, or `null` when it is not tracked yet

post.summary: `POST /api/me/switch-character`, switch the session's active character.

get.summary: `GET /api/me/tokens`, every token on the account, never the secrets.

post.summary: `POST /api/me/tokens`, mint one. The plaintext is in this response and nowhere else.

delete.summary: `DELETE /api/me/tokens/{id}`, and whatever used it is locked out on its next request.

get.summary:
`GET /api/reference-counts`: how much static data is seeded. Changes only when a new
SDE build is loaded.
`GET /api/routing-graph`. Static reference data: cacheable for a day.

`GET /api/server-status`, what Tranquility is doing. Public: the header shows it
signed in or not, and it is the same figure ESI serves to anyone.

`GET /api/share/{token}`: the map a share link leads to, for whoever holds it. A token
that matches nothing, a withdrawn one and a never-shared map all answer `NotFound`, so
the response gives a guesser nothing to work from.

`GET /api/ships/search?q=`, published ship types (SDE category 6) by name, with
hull mass for the manual-jump form. Reference data, no actor check.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Part of a ship type name.

get.summary:
`GET /api/signature-types`: the seeded signature catalog (categories + types with
spawn areas). Reference data, so no actor/role check; cacheable for a day.

`GET /api/skyhooks`, every skyhook currently or shortly raidable. Public EVE data, so
no per-map gating; a session is still required, like the rest of the API.

`GET /api/systems/resolve?ids=a,b,c`, resolve solar system ids to display data for
route rows. Capped at 200 ids.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: Comma-separated solar system ids, at most 200.

get.summary:
`GET /api/systems/search?q=`, search the SDE solar systems by name. Prefix matches rank
first, then shorter names, then alphabetical. Returns nothing for queries under 2 chars.
The ranking query only picks ids; [`systems_for`] builds the rows, so search and resolve
cannot drift apart in what they return.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: What to look for; at least two characters.

get.summary:
`GET /api/threat/{solar_system_id}`: a wormhole system's threat analysis. 404 for
k-space systems (threat is only computed for wormhole space).

post.summary: `POST /api/waypoints`, set a destination/waypoint for one of the caller's characters.

`POST /api/waypoints/all`, set the destination for every online character of the
caller. Best-effort: characters without the scope are skipped; fails only when none
succeed.

AccessEntry.description:
One grant, with the subject's name resolved for display. `name` is `None` when the
subject is an entity we have never cached (a corp nobody on this map belongs to).

expires_at.description: When the grant lapses. `None` lasts until someone revokes it.

entity_name.description: Carried so the receiving side can show who this is without an ESI lookup.

permission.description: `viewer` / `member` / `manager`; the owner row never leaves a map.

AccessSubject.description: A grantable subject from the access-subject search.

oneOf.description:
Initial max ship size, when the client can infer it (e.g. a C13 endpoint is
frigate-sized). `None` = unknown.

mass.description: Explicit mass in kg; wins over the ship type's hull mass.

AddEveScoutToMap.description:
What the client sends to put a hub's holes on the map: the list itself is the server's,
fetched fresh so a stale card cannot map holes that have since collapsed.

x.description: Where to put the hub if it is not on the map yet; the server picks otherwise.

AlertMention.description: Who gets pinged when an alert fires.

AliasScheme.description: How a chain names itself: the sequence an alias suggestion walks.

BackgroundImageUpload.description:
The one part the upload carries. Documentation only: the handler reads the multipart
stream itself.

image.description: PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, at most 8 MiB.

BackgroundMode.description:
How the image sits under the map. `Grid` spans the whole world and moves with the
systems; `Viewport` fills the visible panel and stays put.

CharacterRef.description: One of the user's characters, for the switcher.

is_preferred.description: The one new sessions start as, chosen on the characters page.

solar_system_id.description:
Where the character is right now, when online and tracked. Drives the paste
system-mismatch warning.

CharacterStatus.description: Live status of the active character, for the navbar readout.

CharacterSummary.description: The signed-in character, for the UI's auth state.

wormhole.description: The wormhole code name ("K162"), when one is known.

ConnectionType.description: The kind of edge between two placed systems.

CreatedToken.description: The one response that carries the secret.

DiscordAccount.description: A linked account, as the frontend shows it.

bot.description:
Whether the bot can post to a channel or DM. Needs a bot token on top of the rest;
a plain webhook destination works without it.

linking.description: Whether an account can be linked at all: the OAuth half of the application.

EffectModifier.description:
One buff/debuff a wormhole effect applies, for the node's effect popover. `kind` is the
effect strength tier; `stat` is what it modifies; `value` is the (already-formatted) amount.

EveScoutConnection.description:
A public wormhole out of Thera or Turnur, as EVE Scout's scouts have it. Oriented
hub-first rather than in EVE Scout's in/out terms, and statuses normalized to WormholeSystems's
own vocabulary.

updated_at.description: When a scout last touched it, for the card's freshness stamp.

wormhole_type.description: The wormhole code, e.g. `J377`. Absent while a scout has only half-scanned it.

event_id.description:
The step to move the map onto. `null` rewinds to before the first step, which is a
real destination rather than an omitted field, so it is nullable and not optional.

name.description: Overrides the file's map name when present.

Instance.description:
What this deployment can actually do, so the interface can say what is switched off
rather than offering something that will quietly never arrive. Self-hosters configure
Discord separately from the rest, and most of them do not configure it at all.

JumpDirection.description: Which way a manual jump went, relative to the connection's `from_system` endpoint.

KillParty.description: One entity as a killmail row names it: a portrait, and something to call them.

corporation_name.description: Spelled out for the tooltip; the row has room for a ticker at most.

KillmailScope.description: Which part of the chain the killmails card shows.

LayoutItem.description:
One tile. Minimum sizes deliberately live in the client's panel registry instead, so
tightening one still reaches people who have already saved a layout.

i.description: Panel id. Named `i` to match the stored shape.

allow_layout_override.description: Whether a viewer may pick their own placement instead of the map's.

ghost_unlinked_wormholes.description:
Whether pasting a wormhole signature puts its far side on the map as a ghost.
Map-wide: a ghost is a node everyone on the chain sees.

is_public.description: Whether anyone with the address may watch it, account or no account.

layout.description:
How the chain is placed: `manual` (dragged into shape) or `tree` (drawn from the
connections). Map-wide, so everyone on a chain reads the same picture.

share_token.description:
The secret that lets somebody watch a private map. Only ever sent to a manager:
handing it to a viewer would be handing them the map to pass on.

MapAlert.description: One alert as the settings page shows it.

MapAlertEvent.description: One line of an alert's history.

MapCharacter.description:
An online, tracked character on the map (presence), for the node pilot rows and the
pilots card.

is_docked.description: Docked in a station or structure: on the map, but not on grid.

is_mine.description: One of the viewer's own characters, so their alts can be told apart at a glance.

ship_group_id.description:
The hull's inventory group, so the client can tell a covert-ops scanner from a
combat ship without shipping a table of hull names.

ship_name.description: The name the pilot gave the hull, which is not the hull's type.

jumps_count.description: Full jump-log aggregates (the log itself is fetched separately, capped at 10).

lifetime_hours.description:
How long a hole between these two systems lives, from the class pair (see the
[life-cycle spec](../../docs/processes.md#connection-life-cycle)). `None` for
stargates. With `created_at`, the client's countdown.

oneOf.description:
Wormhole life-cycle state. `None` = unknown; ignored for stargate edges. Synced with
linked signatures by the DB triggers, so reads here already reflect the merged state.

preserve_mass.description: Exclude this hole from mass bookkeeping (legacy flag; stored, not yet consumed).

time_status_updated_at.description: When `time_status` last changed (DB trigger), for "EOL since" displays.

MapEntry.description: A map in the user's list, with their role on it.

is_archived.description: Hidden from this user's list. Per-user, so archiving does not touch anyone else.

is_pinned.description: Whether this user keeps it in the top bar.

last_activity.description: When the chain last changed. `None` for a map nobody has touched yet.

member_count.description: How many people can see it, counting every grant however it was made.

pilots_online.description: Tracked pilots currently online in one of its systems.

oneOf.description: The map's own fields (name / description / image) changed.

A placed system's intel/flags changed (alias, status, occupier, home, pinned): the
position is unchanged, but its details should be refetched.
A connection was added, removed, or had its state changed (incl. trigger-driven sync).
A signature in this system was added, edited, linked, unlinked, or removed.
An access grant changed (membership/roles).
The navigation watchlist changed (entry added/pinned/removed).
The map's ignore list changed: routes and jump tracking steer differently now.

A tracked pilot on this map moved, changed ship, or came on/offline. Sent to the
whole map, unlike the per-user status ping, because everyone's pilot list shows it.
Something died in one of this map's systems.

The command journal grew or an entry was undone, so open clients should refetch
the history (and, after an undo, the map itself).

MapEvent.description:
A change to a map that its viewers should react to. Carries ids, not data: consumers
refetch the named slice.

applied.description: Whether this step is currently in effect, i.e. on the path from a root to the head.

character_name.description: Actor name, or `None` for background tasks.

is_step.description:
Whether this row is a step in the tree. Audit-only rows (background writers) are
shown in the history but cannot be jumped to.

parent_id.description:
The step this one happened on top of. `None` for a root, or once retention has
dropped the ancestor it pointed at.

MapHistory.description: The history as the status bar needs it: the entries plus where the map is sitting.

head_event_id.description: The step the map is on. `None` means every step has been undone.

redo_target.description: The step redo would move to.

undo_target.description: The step undo would move to (`None` when already at a root and nothing is applied).

MapKillmail.description: A killmail as the card shows it: what a row renders, not the raw payload.

MapLayout.description:
Where the nodes get their positions. `Manual` keeps whatever they were dragged to;
`Tree` derives them, and is the map's choice unless it hands it to each viewer.

MapNaming.description:
How a map names its chain. Map-wide rather than per-user: an alias is written on the
map for everyone to read.

alias_scheme.description:
`numeric` (`1`, `11`, `12`) or `alphabetical` (`A`, `AB`, with `H/L/N/P` reserved
for k-space exits).

ignored_alias.description: The alias that sits outside the chain, e.g. `HOME`.

MapSearchHit.description:
One hit from the map command palette. `map_solar_system_id` is set when the system is
already placed; otherwise the hit is an off-map system the palette can add.

note_excerpt.description: The matching slice of the system's notes, when the query hit the notes. Member+ only.

oneOf.description: The organisation that made this system a hit, when the query named a threat group.

solar_system_id.description: `None` for a ghost: the far side of a wormhole nobody has been through yet.

signatures_pasted_at.description:
When a scan was last pasted into this system; `None` if nobody has yet. Hand
edits leave it alone.

oneOf.description: Kill-activity threat (wormhole systems only; `None` for k-space).

wormhole_class_id.description:
Absent on the systems the SDE gives no class, which is not the same as a ghost
having none.

oneOf.description:
The far side of a scanned hole. It draws, moves and is named like any other node,
which is all it has: the rest is looked up from a system it is not yet.

MapSystemView.description:
A placed system enriched with everything a map node displays. Read-only, built by
`get_map` from joins across the SDE + intel + sovereignty tables. Mutations use the lean
[`MapSolarSystem`].

Two shapes, because a node is either a system somebody placed or a hole somebody
scanned: a ghost has no security, statics, or intel, and saying that in the type makes
the check impossible to skip.

background_image_url.description:
Where to fetch the picture behind this user's map from, or `None` for the plain
grid. Changes with every upload, so it is safe to cache hard.

copy_bookmark.description: Put the new connection's bookmark on the clipboard once the jump is mapped.

follow_character.description: Select the system this user's pilot is in as they fly, so the cards follow them.

hidden_panels.description:
Panels this user hides on this map. Empty = the built-in set. A hidden panel keeps
its saved position, so unhiding puts it back where it was.

introduction_confirmed.description: Whether this user has been through the map's introduction.

is_pinned.description: Whether this user keeps the map in the top bar for quick access.

killmail_filter.description: Which half of the chain the killmails card shows.

oneOf.description: Per-breakpoint tile positions. `None` = the built-in arrangement.

This viewer's placement choice, when the map hands it to them. `None` follows the
map's own mode.

preselect_signature.description: Open that prompt with the likeliest signature already chosen.

prompt_for_signature.description: Ask which signature was jumped, rather than mapping the hole unlinked.

route_allow_mass_status.description: Worst wormhole mass still routed through.

route_allow_time_status.description: Worst wormhole lifetime still routed through.

route_use_wormholes.description: Whether the chain's own holes are route edges. Off routes over stargates alone.

security_penalty.description: 0-100, weight of the security preference (legacy `exp(0.15 * penalty)`).

suggest_alias.description: Prefill the jump dialog's alias from the chain's naming scheme.

tracked_character_ids.description: The pilots whose jumps build this map. Empty = the character the session acts as.

MapView.description: The graph as seen by a viewer: the map plus its placed systems and connections.

character_has_access.description:
Whether the *active* character is itself covered by a grant. Access is per-user
(any of their characters), so this can be false while `role` is set: the map is
readable through a different character, but anything tied to the active one
(tracking, waypoints) will not behave as the pilot expects.

role.description: The caller's effective role on this map, for client-side permission gating.

MapWebhook.description: A registered destination, named once and pointed at by any number of alerts.

alert_count.description: How many alerts would stop working if this were deleted.

summary.description:
Enough of the URL to tell two destinations apart, never enough to use one: the URL is
a bearer token for somebody's channel, and every manager reads this list.

MapWebhookRole.description: A registered role, so alerts ping "Scouts" rather than 1189734502938472.

MassStatus.description:
A wormhole's remaining mass, worst last. Variant order is the severity order the
[reconcile-on-link merge](../../docs/database/mapping.md) relies on: `max` is the
worst (= "massed"). Kept in lock-step across a connection and its signatures by the
`map_*_sync` DB triggers (migration 0009).

PastedSignature.description:
One row of a parsed scanner paste. `group` is `None` when the scanner line carried no
classification (legacy: keep whatever the row already has). The catalog type is only
ever client-matched for site categories; wormhole types never come from a paste.

PersonalAccessToken.description: A token as the account settings list it: everything except the secret.

PlanetKind.description:
Which reagent a skyhook's planet yields, the only reason anyone sorts them. Derived from
the type name rather than a list of type ids, so a new variant classifies itself.

ReferenceCounts.description:
How much of New Eden this install has loaded. The landing page states these, so they
are the real contents of this database rather than numbers written into a page.

ResolveGhostSystem.description:
Say which system a ghost turned out to be. `solar_system_id: None` takes it back to a
ghost, and exists as the inverse of the first form rather than as an action of its own.

The rest is what flying the hole taught us about it, carried here rather than sent as
follow-up writes so that one jump stays one undo. All of it is ignored when taking a
node back to a ghost.

raised_by_signature_id.description: Only ever set by the inverse of a resolve; see [`ResolveGhostSystem::unresolve`].

Role.description: A map access role, ordered `Viewer < Member < Manager < Owner`.

RoutePreference.description: What a route is optimised for.

ignored_solarsystems.description: The map's ignore list: routed around by everyone, never placed by jump tracking.

RoutingGraph.description:
The static half of the routing graph, typed and built once: k-space stargate
adjacency (Zarzakh excluded since its gates are faction-gated), per-system security
for the safer/less-secure cost functions, and the station indexes the planner offers.

Rule.description: One rule. The ids within a rule are an OR: "any of these alliances".

map_webhook_id.description: Which registered destination to post to.

origin_solar_system_id.description:
Proximity only: measure from here through the chain instead of from the nearest
mapped system.

url.description: Write-only. Absent on an update keeps the stored one.

ScopeStatus.description: One ESI permission and whether the acting character has consented to it.

SectionCounts.description: What happened to one section of an import.

Sections.description:
Only the sections that were asked for are present; on import, only the requested ones
are read at all, so a broken section nobody selected does not fail the file.

ServerState.description: What the server is doing, as one word for the client to render.

checked_at.description: When we last asked. A stale value here means *our* poller is stuck, not the server.

start_time.description: When this run of the server started, for the uptime readout.

expires_at.description:
When it should lapse. Absent leaves an existing expiry alone; `null` makes the
grant permanent again.

oneOf.description: `None` leaves the edge kind unchanged; `Some(k)` switches wormhole/stargate.

constant_width_enabled.description:
A legacy display setting vector does not have; exported as `false`, ignored on
import, kept so the file validates over there.

rally_solarsystem_id.description:
The single rally point of files written before a map could hold two. Read when
`rally_solarsystem_ids` is absent, never written.

rally_solarsystem_ids.description: Oldest first. On import only the newest two are kept.

ShipSearchResult.description: A ship type matched by the manual-jump ship search.

Side.description: Which end of the killmail to look at.

connection_id.description: The connection this signature is one end of, if linked. Only `wormhole` sigs.

name.description: The raw scanner type name when no catalog type matched.

signature_id.description: The in-game scanner id, e.g. `ABC-123`. Unique per `(map, system)`.

time_status_updated_at.description: When `time_status` last changed (DB trigger), for "EOL since" displays.

SignatureCatalog.description: The full signature catalog, served once and cached client-side.

SignatureCategoryInfo.description: A cosmic-signature category from the seeded catalog.

SignatureGroup.description:
A cosmic-signature group, mirroring [`signature_categories`](../../docs/database/static.md).
Only `Wormhole` signatures carry connection links and the wormhole life-cycle state.

category.description: The category code ("wormhole", "data", ...). Unmatched codes import as `unknown`.

connection_index.description: Index into this file's `connections` array, when the signature is one end of one.

signature_id.description:
The in-game scanner id ("ABC-123"). Legacy allows signatures without one; vector
does not, so those are skipped on import.

type_name.description:
The catalog type by name; both applications seed the catalog from the same data,
so names resolve on either side.

SignatureTypeInfo.description:
A cosmic-signature type from the seeded catalog. `signature` is the wormhole code
(wormhole types only); `target_class` its destination class; `spawn_areas` the system
classes this type can appear in.

total_mass.description: Wormhole physics (joined from `wormhole_types` by code; wormhole types only).

Skyhook.description: A raidable skyhook, enriched with everything a row displays.

planet_name.description: e.g. `4-EP12 VI`, as it reads in the overview.

region_id.description:
Carried so a row can offer the system menu without a second round trip to resolve
the system it already names.

oneOf.description:
Who holds the system. Skyhooks only exist in sovereign nullsec, so this is the
alliance whose toes you are stepping on.

position_x.description:
Null positions mean intel without a placement: the system is not on the canvas,
but its status and notes are kept.

Sovereignty.description:
Who holds sovereignty in a system. The variant *is* the holder kind, so the node knows
which EVE image endpoint to use for the icon; only alliances/corps carry a ticker.

StaleConnection.description: One stale edge, for the status bar's cleanup popover.

critical_since.description: When it was marked critical or expired, whichever it is now.

Static.description:
A static wormhole a system always has, plus the class it leads to (`dest_class` is the
`wormhole_class_id` encoding; `None` for the few codes with no fixed destination) and
the hole physics for the static tooltip.

max_jump_mass.description: Max mass of a single ship per jump, kg.

signature_strength.description: Scan signature strength in percent (higher = easier to scan).

total_mass.description: Total mass the hole can pass before collapsing, kg.

StationGroup.description: A named set of stations: a service, or the corporation that owns them.

oneOf.description: The owning corporation's faction; absent for service groups.

SubjectType.description: What an access grant targets. EVE ids are globally unique across the three.

SystemDetails.description:
A placed system's member-gated intel details (currently just the notes). Viewers never
receive this: the read itself requires Member.

SystemSearchResult.description: A solar system matched by the "add system" search, with just enough to display and pick.

effect_name.description: Wormhole effect, for J-space rows (shown where k-space rows show sovereignty).

statics.description: The statics a wormhole always has. Empty for k-space.

SystemStatus.description:
A placed system's intel status (`map_solar_system_details.status`), set by users.
Matches the legacy vocabulary: `active` = recent activity seen, `empty` = scanned
and found empty.

ThreatAnalysis.description: A wormhole system's threat analysis, for the threat card.

ThreatEntity.description: One organisation in a system's threat top list.

ThreatLevel.description: A wormhole system's kill-activity threat level, from the daily analysis.

ThreatMatch.description: An organisation the threat analysis found operating in a system, as the palette shows it.

kills.description: Kills this organisation has in this system over the analysis window.

TimeStatus.description:
A wormhole's remaining lifetime, worst last. `Eol` ≈ "<4h"; `Critical` ≈ "<1h"
(super-EOL); `Expired` is the in-game "Expired, closure imminent", past any reliable
lifetime. Same severity-ordering / merge semantics as [`MassStatus`].

from_map_solar_system_id.description: The placement the character jumped *from*; it anchors the new system.

signature_pk.description: The signature that turned out to be this hole. `None` = jumped an unscanned one.

x.description: Where to put the new system. The client owns the layout, so it picks the spot.

TransferCounts.description: How much of the map each section would carry, for the export UI. Manager+.

subject_id.description: The character taking it on. They keep no second role: there is one owner.

mass.description: Explicit mass in kg. Absent while the ship type changes → mass re-derives.

UpdateMap.description:
A partial update of a map's fields. `None` leaves a field unchanged; `Some(None)`
explicitly clears a nullable field.

oneOf.description: All-or-nothing: the naming block is edited as one form.

UpdateMapUserSettings.description: Partial update of [`MapUserSettings`]; absent fields stay unchanged.

oneOf.description:
The image itself goes through `/api/maps/{id}/background-image`; this is only how
it is laid out.

introduction_confirmed.description: Stamped server-side, so "when" is the server's clock rather than the browser's.

oneOf.description: Absent leaves it; `null` goes back to following the map.

tracked_character_ids.description: Replaces the set; every id must be one of the caller's characters.

UpdateSignature.description:
A partial edit of a signature. `None` leaves a field unchanged; `Some(None)` clears it.
Changing the group clears the catalog type, the connection link, and any wormhole state
(matching the legacy category select), unless a new type is supplied in the same call.
Editing a linked wormhole's state propagates to its connection via the DB trigger.

signature_id.description: `Some` renames the scanner id (7 chars; duplicate in the system → `Conflict`).

oneOf.description: One of the user's characters had its tracked status updated; refetch.
Tranquility went up, went down, or changed version. Sent to everyone.

UserEvent.description: An event addressed to a single user.

WireLifetime.description:
Legacy's lifetime vocabulary has no "unknown": `healthy` is both vector's `stable` and
its null, and imports as the null (nothing remarkable to show).

WireMassStatus.description:
Legacy's mass vocabulary. Vector's `stable` is legacy's `fresh`, and vector says
"unknown" with a null.

WireShipSize.description: Legacy names hole sizes by the ship class that fits through.

WormholeSize.description:
Max ship-mass class that can transit a wormhole. Ordered most-permissive →
most-restrictive, so `max` (= `Small`) is the "weakest"/worst: the conservative
pick when two ends disagree (they shouldn't: both ends of a hole share a size).

BadRequest.description: The request does not make sense: a missing field, a value out of range, or a body naming a different map than the URL

Conflict.description: The change contradicts the map's current state

Forbidden.description: Signed in, but the role on this map does not allow it

NotFound.description: No such thing, or not one the caller may know about

Unauthorized.description: Nobody is signed in, or the bearer token is unknown, revoked or expired

bearer.description: A personal access token from Settings, API tokens

session.name: ws_session
session.description: The session a browser holds after signing in with EVE

tags.name: maps
tags.description: The maps themselves: list yours, create one, read a whole map in one call, rename or reconfigure it, and who is on it right now. Everything else hangs off a map id from here.

tags.name: access
tags.description: Who may see and edit a map. Roles are granted to a character, corporation or alliance, ownership can be handed over, and a share token gives read-only access without an account.

tags.name: systems
tags.description: The nodes on the map: placing and removing solar systems, moving them, and everything written on a node such as its alias, status, notes, occupier, and the home and rally markers. Also the unresolved hole placeholders and clearing a map.

tags.name: connections
tags.description: The wormholes between two placed systems: adding and removing them, setting mass and lifetime status, the jump log that feeds the mass estimate, and pruning connections nobody has used in a while.

tags.name: signatures
tags.description: Scan results per system: pasting the probe scanner, editing single signatures, and linking a wormhole signature to the connection it turned out to be. The type catalogue for the pickers lives here too.

tags.name: tracking
tags.description: Jump tracking on behalf of a pilot: telling the map a character moved from one system to another, so the hole gets mapped and linked the way the automatic tracker would.

tags.name: history
tags.description: The map's undo history: the event log, stepping back and forward, and jumping to a point in it. Every write elsewhere lands here as an event.

tags.name: watchlist
tags.description: Systems a map keeps an eye on for routing: the list, adding and removing entries, and pinning the ones that matter most.

tags.name: ignored systems
tags.description: Systems the whole map routes around and never auto-places, kept on the server so route planning, Discord routes and alerts all agree. Manager only.

tags.name: eve scout
tags.description: The public holes out of Thera and Turnur as EVE Scout's scouts report them, and putting one hub's connections on the map in one step.

tags.name: alerts
tags.description: What a map watches for and where it tells people: proximity, killmail and jump-range alerts, their delivery to Discord channels or DMs, the roles that can be mentioned, and the webhooks a map posts to.

tags.name: killmails
tags.description: Recent kills in and around the chain, as the map's killmail feed shows them.

tags.name: search
tags.description: Searching within one map: systems, aliases, signatures and notes in one query.

tags.name: transfer
tags.description: Moving a map between instances: export to a file, import into an existing map, or create a new map from a file. The format is the one the legacy app reads and writes.

tags.name: user settings
tags.description: One person's preferences on one map: routing tolerances, what the tracker does for them, which panels are shown and where. Nothing here affects other viewers.

tags.name: background image
tags.description: A picture behind one viewer's map: upload, fetch and remove, with the layout mode set through user settings.

tags.name: identity
tags.description: The signed-in user: their characters, which one they act as, ESI scopes, Discord link, and setting in-game waypoints through ESI.

tags.name: tokens
tags.description: Personal access tokens for scripts. Managed only from a browser session; the plaintext is shown once at creation.

tags.name: reference
tags.description: Static and instance-wide data the frontend needs: the universe graph for routing, wormhole effects, signature types, threat analysis, skyhook timers, server status and the instance's configuration.
